answer: In this PoA design, each identity is bound to a Wesolowski VDF whose output requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with every result feeding the next. An attacker can assign separate clones to different GPUs, but cannot parallelize the dependency chain or reduce its physical delay for any one clone, so simulating many identities multiplies the required work. Labels such as cipher, velvet, or canyon provide no shortcut.
